Represented space immediately surrounding the body and relevant to near-body action and multisensory integration.
A spatial reference frame centered on the current embodied perspective.
A dimension describing positive/negative or attractive/aversive affective valuation under a declared scale.
A dimension of physiological or experiential activation distinct from valence.
A valuation/control dimension indicating pressure for rapid allocation of processing or action resources.
The degree to which a state is evaluated as relevant to possible harm or loss under a declared model.
The degree to which a state concerns maintained attachment relations or their disruption.
The degree to which a state concerns predicted reward, preference satisfaction, or valued outcome.
The represented object, state, relation, or possibility toward which an affective valuation is directed.
Inference that an affective state is present in a person or system; it requires evidence and must not be silently manufactured.
Use of an explicit or measured affective variable to alter resource allocation, salience, recall, inhibition, exploration, or consolidation.
A target-relative multidimensional mapping of valuation variables such as valence, arousal, urgency, threat, attachment, and reward relevance.
Priority assigned to content partly through affective valuation without converting that priority into truth or authority.
A relatively sustained affective background state that can modulate processing across multiple targets.
A coordinated episode involving appraisal, bodily change, action tendency, expression, and/or experience; exact components depend on the model.
The experienced aspect of an affective or bodily state; not every computational valuation variable establishes feeling.
An aversive sensory and affective experience associated with actual or potential tissue damage or described in those terms; mechanisms and reports require empirical context.
A positively valenced experiential quality that can arise from diverse sensory, cognitive, social, or motivational processes.
An affective state commonly involving aversion and rejection tendencies; its sensory, moral, and social forms should be distinguished.
A self-evaluative affective state involving perceived negative evaluation of the self in relation to standards or others.
A self-evaluative affective state focused more specifically on actions, omissions, or responsibility for harm than on global self-worth.
An affective state often associated with perceived obstruction, injustice, threat, or norm violation and increased action readiness.
An affective state often associated with loss, reduced reward, or withdrawal tendencies; it is not identical to clinical depression.
A positively valenced affective state associated with reward, connection, relief, or valued outcomes.
A response to unexpected information or prediction violation; valence may be positive, negative, or neutral.
A relational expectation that another agent or system will behave reliably or cooperatively under relevant conditions.
Capacity to represent or respond to another agent experiential or affective state while maintaining self-other distinction.
Concern for another suffering combined with motivation toward helpful or protective response; distinct from emotional contagion.
Affective convergence between agents without necessarily representing the other state as other.
A sustained relational organization in which another agent or object has enduring regulatory and motivational significance.
An aversive experience associated with perceived insufficiency of desired social connection; distinct from objective social isolation.
A low-urgency affective condition that may involve reduced arousal or threat relevance without implying absence of attention.
Simultaneous incompatible valuations or action tendencies associated with the same or competing targets.
A represented tendency toward a possible state or outcome; desire alone need not establish intention or commitment.
A comparative valuation ordering among alternatives under a declared context.
Processes that energize, select, or sustain goal-directed behavior or cognition.
An internal representation of a target state or maintained constraint.
Persistence of a goal representation so it continues to constrain ongoing processing.
Competition or incompatibility among simultaneously active goals.
Competition or incompatibility among valuations relevant to a decision or trajectory.
Stabilization of a selected intention or course of action against competing alternatives.
A transition in which one option or policy is selected under a declared decision process.
The selected option among represented alternatives; choice does not by itself establish metaphysical free will.
A process determining which available action or policy is executed or further prepared.
A system-caused change in body, environment, communication, or internal control state under a declared agency model.
A state in which action-related processes are prepared for rapid execution.
